targets.review_note: Treat knowledge arrival as a time-dependent shortest-path problem with waiting allowed and zero communication delay. For a robot informed at time t, scan two piecewise-linear routes over their merged segment boundaries to find the earliest later contact. Relative squared distance is a quadratic; test immediate contact, otherwise solve the entering root using a numerically stable positive-root formula and clip only negligible floating boundary error under the stated event separation guarantee. Dijkstra is valid because earliest-contact time is nondecreasing in the information start time (FIFO with waiting). Relaxing every uninformed robot propagates simultaneous multi-robot contacts and later mobile relays, while already informed robots retain data forever after separation. Respect velocity-on-the-preceding-interval input semantics, include contacts at T, and output only first-robot information recipients in dictionary order.
